To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) for the LCLMS adaptive algorithm, the step-size range for binary input is larger than that for jointly Gaussian input, and (b) the step-size range can be further increased by employing a modified LCLMS algorithm.

(1) the step-size range for LCLMS with PR equalization and binary inputs is larger than that for LCLMS without PR equalization and with Gaussian input signals, (2) for a given step size, the LCLMS with Gaussian input signals is more stable than that with binary input signals, and (3) the stability of the LCLMSE algorithm is not affected by the number of constraints.

(i) the LCLMS adaptive algorithm is stable if the equalizer step-size is chosen within [0,2) and the PR step-size within [0,1) when the input is binary, and (ii) the LCLM algorithm is stable if both the equalizer and PR step-sizes are chosen within [0,(1+sqrt(5)/2) when the input has a Gaussian distribution

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LCLMS with a binary data stream has a larger step-size range than the LCLMS in the Gaussian case, but the step-size range of LCLMS in either case is still too small for practical applications.
the LCLMS is a stable and convergent algorithm for jointly adapting equalizer and target in PR channels, with binary data.
the LCLMS adaptive algorithm is not stable for PR equalization when the equalizer and PR-target step sizes are chosen independently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LCLMS adaptive algorithm is stable and converges to the desired PR equalization solution, when the step size of the equalizer update is within a certain range.
the LCLMS with PR target and binary input has the same convergence behavior as that with Gaussian input, except that its step-size range is larger.
, the step sizes required to guarantee convergence of LCLMS for PR recording channels are larger than the corresponding ones for LMS with Gaussian input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LCLMS with distinct step sizes is stable for binary input signals, provided the step-size range is sufficiently large.
the LCLMS adaptive algorithm can achieve fast convergence for binary input, provided the PR target is designed to be sufficiently robust.
the step size required to guarantee convergence for LCLMS with PR equalization is larger than that for conventional LMS.
